findings.quote: That a chain of dams along a single tributary leaves the valley below worse off in a big storm than having no beavers at all.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: two options fall out on form alone. D is an absolute worse-than-nothing overclaim, and A reduces a 'mainly about' answer to a measurement-quality quibble about volunteers with tape measures — neither shape survives as a main-idea key. That leaves B vs C, which are not decidable blind.

findings.quote: Once every pond has filled the catchment passes the water on much as it did before the beavers.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE/PARTIALLY (blind pick D): A is hydrologically backwards on ordinary reasoning (headwaters are farther from the gauge, so their water arrives later, not sooner) and C answers a rain question with beaver behaviour, a domain mismatch. D is the standard saturation outcome any reader with basic knowledge would expect. B remains substantive, so the item is narrowed rather than decided.

findings.quote: Water from different tributaries needs different amounts of time to arrive, so spread-out dams keep the peaks from coinciding.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, with a stem-entailment component: the stem supplies the premise ('tributaries are of very unequal length') and B's first clause is close to a restatement of it. C is self-defeating (the same dams cannot hold appreciably more water because they sit on one tributary) and A does not follow from length at all. D is a genuine competing consequence of the same premise, so B is favoured but not decided blind.

findings.quote: He finds the campaign sentimental and the flood benefit too slight to be worth the trouble of measuring.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: an attitude stem with two eliminable extremes — A endorses the campaigner's slogan verbatim and D is dismissive of a study the writer is reporting at length. The remaining B and C are both qualified middle positions pointing opposite ways, so the key is not decided blind.

findings.quote: Because the bands come from the way the grass is lying, so the same rows are read the other way round from the far side.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick A): mown stripes are a light-reflection effect of grass bent in opposite directions, and the light/dark pattern reverses when viewed from the opposite end — common general knowledge. The distractors are real misconceptions rather than filler (D is the widely held 'two cutting heights' belief, C the lighting explanation), so this is a genuine comprehension item whose key happens to be true in the world; routed to adjudication, not killed.

findings.quote: How gently it stops a falling head, judged against the tallest equipment above it, and whether it is kept at that depth.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE/PARTIALLY (blind pick C): impact attenuation measured against the critical fall height, plus maintained depth, is the actual playground-safety standard, so domain knowledge names the key. There is also a mild form asymmetry — A, B and D share a 'criterion, since <single-cause reason>' shape while C alone states a measured criterion plus an upkeep condition. The distractors are substantive site considerations a passage could plausibly endorse, so this is flag rather than a structural kill.

findings.quote: can fail badly under a three-meter tower
findings.note: class 4: unit/house-style incoherence. The passage sets fall height in metric ('three-meter') but reports depth loss in imperial ('two inches short of it') with no conversion, and uses US spellings ('meter', 'fiber') throughout; a copy desk standardises one system per piece. Editor's rewrite: 'can fail badly under a ten-foot tower' (with 'two inches' kept) or 'three-metre tower' with 'five centimetres short'.

findings.quote: a bed that met its rating in May may be two inches short of it by September
findings.note: class 3: loose pronoun reference — a bed is short of the depth the rating assumes, not short of the rating itself, so 'short of it' collocates badly with 'rating'. Editor's rewrite: 'a bed that met its rating in May may be two inches below the depth that rating assumes by September'.

findings.quote: a bed that passes under a low toddler frame can fail badly under a three-meter tower
findings.note: class 4: unit-system incoherence inside a short passage. The spelling is American throughout ('meter', 'wood fiber'), and US playground-safety practice (ASTM F1292) states fall heights in feet, yet the tower here is metric while the surfacing depth two sentences later is imperial ('two inches short of it by September'). A copy editor at any of the model publications would harmonise the two. Editor's rewrite: 'can fail badly under a ten-foot tower' (or keep metric and make the depth 'five centimetres short of it').

findings.quote: children kick them out from under the swings, which is exactly where they are wanted
findings.note: class 3: squinting relative. The antecedent 'which' requires is the ground *under* the swings, but the nearest noun phrase is governed by 'out from under', so the sentence literally says the place the chips are kicked out of is the place they are wanted; the reader recovers, but pauses. Editor's rewrite: 'children kick them out from under the swings - and under the swings is exactly where they are needed'.

findings.quote: can fail badly under a three-meter tower
findings.note: class 4: the passage is otherwise consistently American ("fiber", "meter") and closes with an imperial measure ("two inches short of it by September"); a copy editor at a US title would not let a metric tower height and an imperial depth loss stand four sentences apart. Editor's rewrite: 'can fail badly under a ten-foot tower' (or convert the later figure to '5 cm short').

findings.quote: Genomgången visade framför allt att distriktets bokbidrag med tiden kom att betalas ut i pengar i stället för i böcker.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: D answers a durability question with an unrelated accounting change and drops out on form. B and C are then a minimal pair differing only in a scope qualifier ('oavsett om de samlades i hemmen eller i logelokalen' vs 'främst de som samlades i hemmen'), which narrows the field to two without deciding between them blind.

findings.quote: Den låter en enskild cirkel åskådliggöra det materialet i övrigt bara antyder, utan att gälla som bevis.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: a 'what function does this anecdote serve' stem where D is the only epistemically hedged option (illustrates but does not prove) against A's absolute 'tyngsta belägg'. That is a familiar test-wise lean toward D, but B (reliability of late minutes) and C (an exception case) are substantive functions a passage could genuinely assign, so it is narrowed, not decided.

findings.quote: Vad som lästes tycks ha betytt mindre än hur ansvaret fördelades, men materialet medger ingen visshet.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: in a 'vilket påstående överensstämmer bäst' set, B is the sole qualified statement among three absolutes — A's single-cause 'mer än annat avgjorde', C's 'genomgående' plus a normative 'borde', D's blanket 'säger något säkert'. The hedge-among-absolutes shape gives a strong blind lean to B. Flagged rather than killed because this option profile is standard in authentic HP items and a passage can still be what decides it.

findings.quote: Protokollen har bevarats så ojämnt att jämförelser mellan olika slags cirklar inte säger något säkert om uthålligheten.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the source-criticism paragraph is genuinely on this option's side — "Materialet har sina hål. För krigsåren saknas listor på flera håll, och vem ledaren var anges långt ifrån alltid", "Att kalla en sådan uppskattning ett mått är att ta i", plus Hasselgren's confounding and time-span objections and Ödmark's own "en tendens är ingen förklaring". A strong reader can build a case. It is nevertheless beatable: the text attributes the uncertainty mainly to confounding and to leader attribution, not to uneven preservation, and it explicitly refuses D's conclusion — "håller fast vid att mönstret återkommer i för många orter för att avfärdas". Key B carries the same hedge ("materialet medger ingen visshet") while also stating the text's central finding ("Mönstret ... gäller ansvaret snarare än stoffet"), so the prompt's "bäst" delimiter settles it. Attractive, not a double-key.

findings.quote: De flesta striderna uppstod när två gator med samma namn låg inom samma utryckningsområde.
findings.note: PARTIALLY/WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: D describes an administrative duplication problem rather than a naming dispute and drops out on form; A is the null-result option that negates the very qualifier B carries. B and C are exact mirrors, and ordinary knowledge of such disputes (people object to losing a familiar address) leans toward B. Narrowed to a two-way lean, not decided blind.

findings.quote: I nybyggda områden, där gatorna knappt hunnit få någon muntlig historia, kom det knappt några invändningar alls.
findings.note: class 6: 'knappt' repeated twice within one sentence in two different senses ('barely had time to' / 'hardly any'); an edited-sakprosa copy editor would break the echo. Native alternative: '... där gatorna ännu inte hunnit få någon muntlig historia, kom det nästan inga invändningar alls.'

findings.quote: Ett förslag som kommer med skäl går att bemöta i sak.
findings.note: class 2: borderline calque of English 'comes with reasons (attached)'. Swedish 'komma med' means to put forward (someone comes with a proposal), not to be accompanied by. Native alternative: 'Ett förslag som motiveras går att bemöta i sak.'

findings.quote: eftersom en gammal adress bör få vara ifred från politiken
findings.note: class 1: 'ifred' written as one word; standard orthography is the two-word 'i fred' (lämna ngn i fred). Native alternative: 'bör få vara i fred från politiken'.

findings.quote: eftersom alla gator förr eller senare blir vardagsspråk
findings.note: class 6: category slip — a street cannot become everyday language, its name can. Native alternative: 'eftersom alla gatunamn förr eller senare blir vardagsspråk'.

findings.quote: Ett förslag som kommer med skäl går att bemöta i sak. Ett som kommer med enbart ett protokollnummer går bara att bli arg på.
findings.note: class 2: 'komma med' with an inanimate subject in the sense 'be accompanied by / be supplied with' is the documented English 'comes with' calque (the type Språkrådet warns about in 'programmet kommer med en handbok'); native Swedish reserves 'komma med X' for an animate agent putting X forward, so a förslag cannot itself 'komma med skäl'. Native alternative: 'Ett förslag som motiveras går att bemöta i sak. Ett som bara åtföljs av ett protokollnummer går bara att bli arg på.'

findings.quote: I nybyggda områden, där gatorna knappt hunnit få någon muntlig historia, kom det knappt några invändningar alls.
findings.note: class 6: 'knappt' repeated within one sentence in two different senses ('barely had time' vs 'hardly any'); an editor of sakprosa would break the echo. Native alternative: '... där gatorna ännu inte hunnit få någon muntlig historia, kom det knappt några invändningar alls.'

findings.quote: eftersom alla gator förr eller senare blir vardagsspråk
findings.note: class 6: category mismatch — a gata cannot 'bli vardagsspråk'; it is the name that enters everyday speech. Native alternative: 'eftersom alla gatunamn förr eller senare går in i vardagsspråket'.

findings.quote: eftersom en gammal adress bör få vara ifred från politiken
findings.note: class 1/6: 'ifred' as one word is nonstandard in modern edited Swedish (SAOL has 'i fred'), and 'vara i fred från politiken' is a strained collocation. Native alternative: 'bör få vara i fred' / 'bör slippa politiken'.

findings.quote: I nybyggda områden, där gatorna knappt hunnit få någon muntlig historia, kom det knappt några invändningar alls.
findings.note: class 6: 'knappt' twice in one sentence in two different senses ('barely had time to' / 'hardly any'); grammatical and idiomatic but a copy editor would break the echo. Native alternative: 'där gatorna ännu inte hunnit få någon muntlig historia, kom det knappt några invändningar alls'.

findings.quote: Ur vid platser med fasta avgångstider gick alltid rätt, medan varje ur på en kyrka eller bankfasad hade stannat.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: B is the absolute-overclaim twin of C ('alltid', 'varje') and falls out on form; D reports an unrelated interwar finding and is off-frame for an inventory result. That leaves A and C as direct mirrors, a 50/50 that the passage still has to decide.

findings.quote: Uret var främst en gemensam överenskommelse om tiden, och det förföll när färre verksamheter behövde samla folk samtidigt.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: C is a bare cliché absolute ('fyller inte längre någon praktisk uppgift'), D reverses a causal chain in an implausible direction (unmaintained clocks causing operators to abandon timetables), and B narrows the whole text to an administrative purpose. A is the only thesis-shaped option left, so the blind lean is strong. Flagged rather than killed: this profile is common in authentic 'överensstämmer bäst' items and the passage remains what grounds it.

findings.quote: Sedan alla bär en klocka i fickan fyller stadens offentliga ur inte längre någon praktisk uppgift.
findings.note: class 2/3: causal English 'since' rendered as Swedish temporal 'sedan'. Subordinating 'sedan' requires a completed event ('sedan han kommit hem'), not a stative present. Native alternative: 'Nu när alla bär en klocka i fickan ...' or 'Sedan alla börjat bära en klocka i fickan ...'.

findings.quote: vilka av städernas ur som borde byggnadsminnesmärkas
findings.note: class 1: non-standard derivation blending 'byggnadsminne' and 'minnesmärka'. The established Swedish term is 'byggnadsminnesförklara' (colloquially 'k-märka'). Native alternative: 'som borde byggnadsminnesförklaras'.

findings.quote: vilka av städernas ur som borde byggnadsminnesmärkas
findings.note: class 1: wrong derivation — the established Swedish verb is 'byggnadsminnesförklara' (noun 'byggnadsminnesförklaring'); 'byggnadsminnesmärka' is a blend with 'k-märka/minnesmärke' that occurs only in careless usage and would not survive a copy edit of edited sakprosa. Native alternative: 'vilka av städernas ur som borde byggnadsminnesförklaras'.

findings.quote: Ekvalls inventering gjordes för att avgöra vilka av städernas ur som borde byggnadsminnesmärkas.
findings.note: class 1: 'byggnadsminnesmärkas' is a lay blend of 'byggnadsminne' and 'minnesmärka'; it occurs in loose journalistic Swedish but the term of art in edited sakprosa is 'byggnadsminnesförklaras' (colloquially 'k-märkas'). Native alternative: 'vilka av städernas ur som borde byggnadsminnesförklaras'.
